facts.statement: Vulcanodon lived during the Sinemurian to Pliensbachian stages of the Early Jurassic.
facts.quote: fossil_range: Sinemurian-Pliensbachian,

facts.statement: The genus Vulcanodon was named and described by Michael Raath in 1972.
facts.quote: authority: Raath, 1972

facts.statement: Vulcanodon was discovered in Zimbabwe in 1969.
facts.quote: Discovered in 1969 in Zimbabwe

facts.statement: The only known species of Vulcanodon is Vulcanodon karibaensis.
facts.quote: The only known species is V. karibaensis.

facts.statement: Vulcanodon measured approximately 11 meters in length, making it smaller than most other sauropods.
facts.quote: It was smaller than most other sauropods, measuring approximately 11 m in length.

facts.statement: In 2010, Gregory S. Paul estimated Vulcanodon's length at 11 meters and its weight at 3.5 tonnes.
facts.quote: In 2010, Gregory S. Paul estimated its length at 11 metres (36.1 ft), its weight at 3.5 tonnes (3.9 short tons).

facts.statement: In 2018, researchers estimated Vulcanodon's body mass to be 10.3 metric tonnes.
facts.quote: However, in 2018, researchers have estimated a greater body mass of 10.3 MT.

facts.statement: The thighbone of Vulcanodon was 110 centimeters long.
facts.quote: The thighbone was 110 cm long.

facts.statement: Vulcanodon was fully quadrupedal with limb proportions intermediate between its prosauropod ancestors and later sauropods.
facts.quote: While Vulcanodon already was fully quadrupedal (four-legged), its limb proportions were intermediate between those of its prosauropod ancestors and those of later, more derived sauropods.

facts.statement: Vulcanodon had sturdy, column-like limbs with forelimbs reaching 76% of the hindlimb length.
facts.quote: Vulcanodons limbs were sturdy and column-like, and its forelimbs were already proportionally long, reaching 76% of hindlimb length.

facts.statement: Vulcanodon possessed a sacrum made of four fused vertebrae, whereas prosauropods had only three.
facts.quote: The sacrum was made out of four fused sacral vertebrae; "prosauropods" possessed only three sacrals.

facts.statement: The hallux of Vulcanodon featured a large, laterally flattened claw similar to that of prosauropods.
facts.quote: The hallux (the first toe of the foot) showed a large claw that was flattened laterally, as seen in "prosauropods".

facts.statement: The claws on the second and third toes of Vulcanodon were unusual, being nail-like and broader than deep.
facts.quote: However, the claws of the second and third toe were unusual in being nail-like and broader than deep.

facts.statement: Vulcanodon had semiplantigrade feet where digits and part of the metatarsals contacted the ground, a derived feature absent in basal sauropods like Isanosaurus.
facts.quote: The feet of Vulcanodon were semiplantigrade as in later sauropods (where both the digits and part of the metatarsals contact the ground), a derived feature not found in more basal sauropods like Isanosaurus.

facts.statement: The first bone of Vulcanodon was found by B. A. Gibson in July 1969.
facts.quote: The first bone was found by B. A. Gibson of the town of Kariba in July 1969

facts.statement: Vulcanodon was formally named and described in July 1972 by paleontologist Michael Raath.
facts.quote: The find was formally named and described in July 1972 by paleontologist Michael Raath.

facts.statement: The name Vulcanodon refers to the knife-shaped teeth found near the skeleton, which were later identified as belonging to a theropod scavenger rather than the sauropod itself.
facts.quote: The name Vulcanodon (lat. Vulcanus – Roman god of fire; gr. odon – "tooth") points to the fact that the skeleton was found in sandstone, that was at the time misinterpreted to be part of the Batoka Formation but is actually part of the Forest Sandstone lays a few metres below the lava flows of the Batoka Formation, and emphasizes the peculiar knife-shaped teeth that are now known to belong to a theropod.

facts.statement: Vulcanodon was one of the first dinosaurs discovered in Zimbabwe.
facts.quote: It was one of the first dinosaurs found in Zimbabwe.

facts.statement: The Vulcanodon remains are currently stored in the Natural History Museum of Zimbabwe in Bulawayo.
facts.quote: Today, the Vulcanodon remains are stored in the Natural History Museum of Zimbabwe in Bulawayo.

facts.statement: Raath (1972) hypothesized that nine carnivorous teeth found near the pelvis indicated the carcass was in a 'death pose' with the head and neck bent backwards.
facts.quote: Raath (1972) noted the discovery of nine fragmentary carnivorous teeth near the pelvic region of the skeleton. He argued that the Vulcanodon carcass might have been embedded with the head and neck bended backwards above the pelvis, a posture called death pose that is frequently seen in dinosaur skeletons.

facts.statement: Cooper (1984) demonstrated that the carnivorous teeth found near the skeleton belonged to a theropod scavenger, not Vulcanodon.
facts.quote: However, as shown by Cooper (1984), these teeth do not pertain to Vulcanodon but to a theropod dinosaur that may have scavenged on the Vulcanodon carcass.

facts.statement: Vulcanodon and Tazoudasaurus were unified in the family Vulcanodontidae, though this classification is not universally accepted.
facts.quote: Upon the discovery of the related Tazoudasaurus, both animals were unified in the family Vulcanodontidae, although this has not been universally accepted.

facts.statement: Vulcanodon was originally thought to be a prosauropod and potentially omnivorous due to knife-shaped teeth found near its fossils.
facts.quote: Originally, this genus was believed to be a "prosauropod" because of the knife-shaped teeth found near its fossils, which fit in with the idea that they were omnivorous.

facts.statement: Scientists now know that the knife-shaped teeth belonged to an unidentified theropod scavenger, confirming Vulcanodon as a true sauropod.
facts.quote: Scientists now know that the teeth belonged to an unidentified theropod that may have scavenged on the Vulcanodon carcass, which is now known to be a true sauropod.

facts.statement: The species Vulcanodon karibaensis was discovered in 1969 in Zimbabwe.
facts.quote: Descubierto en 1969 en Zimbabue

facts.statement: Vulcanodon lived during the early Jurassic period, approximately 183 to 175 million years ago in the Toarcian stage.
facts.quote: vivió a principios del período Jurásico hace unos 183 a 175 millones de años durante el Toarciense

facts.statement: Vulcanodon was smaller than most other sauropods, measuring approximately 11 meters in length.
facts.quote: Era más pequeño que la mayoría de los otros saurópodos y medía aproximadamente 11 metros de largo

facts.statement: As a ground-dwelling quadrupedal herbivore, Vulcanodon exhibited the typical sauropod body plan with pillar-like legs and long necks and tails.
facts.quote: Como un herbívoro cuadrúpedo que habita en el suelo, Vulcanodon ya mostraba el típico plan corporal de saurópodo con patas en forma de columna y cuello y cola largos

facts.statement: The known fossil material consists of a fragmentary skeleton including most of the pelvic girdle, hind legs, forearms, and tail, but lacking the torso, neck vertebrae, and skull.
facts.quote: Se conoce a partir de un esqueleto fragmentario que incluye gran parte de la cintura pélvica , las patas traseras, los antebrazos y la cola, pero que carece del tronco y las vértebras del cuello , así como del cráneo

facts.statement: The genus was originally thought to be a prosauropod because knife-shaped teeth found near the fossils suggested an omnivorous diet.
facts.quote: Originalmente, se creía que este género era un prosaurópodo debido a los dientes en forma de cuchillo encontrados cerca de sus fósiles, lo que encaja con la idea de que los prosaurópodos eran omnívoros

facts.statement: Scientists now know that the knife-shaped teeth belonged to an unidentified theropod that may have scavenged the Vulcanodon carcass.
facts.quote: Los científicos ahora saben que los dientes pertenecían a un terópodo no identificado que pudo haber hurgado en el cadáver de Vulcanodon

facts.statement: Vulcanodon fossils come from the "Vulcanodon beds," a sediment unit within the Batoka Formation composed primarily of flood basalts.
facts.quote: Vulcanodon comes from the "Vulcanodon beds", a fossil-bearing sediment unit within the Batoka Formation, which is composed primarily of flood basalts

facts.statement: Cooper (1984) pointed out that Vulcanodon lived in a desert-like environment and therefore must have been terrestrial, indicating that large sauropod body size did not evolve as an adaptation to aquatic life.
facts.quote: In 1984, Cooper pointed out that Vulcanodon, the most primitive sauropod known at that time, lived in a desert like environment and therefore must have been terrestrial

facts.statement: It is debated whether the sibling relationship between Tazoudasaurus and Vulcanodon is confirmed, as other analyses could not verify it.
facts.quote: However, this sibling relationship between Tazoudasaurus and Vulcanodon could not be confirmed by other analyses

facts.statement: In 2018, low water levels in Lake Kariba allowed study confirming the holotype came from the uppermost Forest Sandstone, dating from the Rhaetian to the Pliensbachian with a Sinemurian-Pliensbachian midpoint.
facts.quote: In 2018 was revelated that as in 2016 Lake Kariba hosted record-low water levels the unit were accessible to be studied and confirmed that the holotype came from the uppermost Forest Sandstone, being as old as the Rhaetian or as young as the Pliensbachian, with a Sinemurian-Pliensbachian Midpoint

facts.statement: In 2010, Gregory S. Paul estimated Vulcanodon's length at 11 meters and its weight at 3.5 tons.
facts.quote: En 2010, Gregory S. Paul estimó su longitud en 11 metros y su peso en 3,5 toneladas.

facts.statement: In 2018, researchers estimated a higher body mass of 10.3 tons.
facts.quote: Sin embargo, en 2018, los investigadores han estimado una mayor masa corporal de 10,3 toneladas.

facts.statement: The femur measured 110 centimeters in length.
facts.quote: El fémur medía 110 centímetros de largo.

facts.statement: As one of the oldest and most basal sauropods, it is important for understanding the early evolution of this group.
facts.quote: Como uno de los saurópodos más antiguos y basales, es importante para comprender la evolución temprana de este grupo.

facts.statement: Although Vulcanodon was fully quadrupedal, its limb proportions were intermediate between its prosauropod ancestors and more derived sauropods.
facts.quote: Si bien Vulcanodon ya era completamente cuadrúpedo, de cuatro patas, las proporciones de sus extremidades eran intermedias entre las de sus ancestros prosaurópodos y las de los saurópodos posteriores más derivados.

facts.statement: Its forelimbs were more similar to later sauropods than to basal sauropodomorphs because they were straight, much more gracile, and the proximal end of the ulna had a V-shape.
facts.quote: Sus extremidades anteriores eran mucho más similares a los saurópodos posteriores que a los sauropodomorfos basales porque son rectas, mucho más gráciles y el extremo proximal del cúbito tiene forma de v.

facts.statement: Unfortunately, no skull or neck of Vulcanodon is known, although otherwise it is very well known.
facts.quote: Desafortunadamente, ningún cráneo o cuello de Vulcanodon es conocido, aunque por lo demás es muy conocido.

facts.statement: Vulcanodon's limbs were robust and pillar-like, and its forelimbs were already proportionally long, reaching 76% of the length of the hind limbs.
facts.quote: Las extremidades de Vulcanodon eran robustas y parecidas a columnas, y sus extremidades anteriores ya eran proporcionalmente largas, alcanzando el 76% de la longitud de las extremidades posteriores.

facts.statement: The sacrum was formed by four fused sacral vertebrae.
facts.quote: El sacro estaba formado por cuatro vértebras sacras fusionadas.

facts.statement: The tail vertebrae already showed an incipient excavation on their lateral sides, saving weight and giving them a carved appearance when viewed from below.
facts.quote: Los cuerpos vertebrales de la cola ya mostraban una incipiente excavación de sus lados laterales, ahorrando peso y dándoles un aspecto entallado visto desde abajo.

facts.statement: One of these characteristics is that the ilion's brevis platform has a fossa, which is not found in any other derived sauropod.
facts.quote: Una de esas características es que la plataforma brevis del ilion tiene una fosa, que no se encuentra en ningún otro saurópodo derivado.

facts.statement: The hallux, the first toe, showed a large laterally flattened claw, as seen in "prosauropods".
facts.quote: El hallux, el primer dedo del pie, mostraba una gran garra aplanada lateralmente, como se ve en los "prosaurópodos".

facts.statement: However, the claws of the second and third toes were unusual for being like nails and wider than deep.
facts.quote: Sin embargo, las garras del segundo y tercer dedo del pie eran inusuales por ser como uñas y más anchas que profundas.

facts.statement: This feature was also found in Tazoudasaurus, a genus probably closely related, but is absent in all other sauropods.
facts.quote: Esta característica también se encontró en Tazoudasaurus, género probablemente estrechamente relacionado, pero está ausente en todos los demás saurópodos.

facts.statement: Vulcanodon is known only from a single locality on an island in Lake Kariba, the world's largest artificial lake, in northern Zimbabwe, formerly Rhodesia.
facts.quote: Vulcanodon se conoce solo de una sola localidad en una isla en el lago Kariba, el lago artificial más grande del mundo, en el norte de Zimbabue, antes Rhodesia.

facts.statement: The first bone was found by B. A. Gibson from the city of Kariba in July 1969, and an excavation team collected the specimen in October 1969, March 1970, and May 1970.
facts.quote: El primer hueso fue encontrado por B. A. Gibson de la ciudad de Kariba en julio de 1969, y un equipo de excavación recolectó el espécimen en octubre de 1969, marzo de 1970 y mayo de 1970.

facts.statement: The find was formally named and described in July 1972 by paleontologist Michael Raath.
facts.quote: El hallazgo fue nombrado y descrito formalmente en julio de 1972 por el paleontólogo Michael Raath.

facts.statement: The skeleton, catalog number QG24, was found eroding on the slope of a hill and was partially eroded by surface exposure and plant roots.
facts.quote: El esqueleto, número de catálogo QG24, se ha encontrado erosionándose en la ladera de una colina y fue parcialmente erosionado por la exposición de la superficie y las raíces de las plantas.

facts.statement: It includes the pelvis and sacrum, most of the left hind limb and foot, a right femur, and twelve anterior tail vertebrae.
facts.quote: Incluye la pelvis y el sacro, la mayor parte de la extremidad trasera izquierda y el pie, un fémur derecho y doce vértebras anteriores de la cola.

facts.statement: Today, Vulcanodon remains are stored in the Zimbabwe National Museum in Bulawayo.
facts.quote: Hoy en día, los restos de Vulcanodon se almacenan en el Museo de Historia Natural de Zimbabue en Bulawayo.

facts.statement: In 1972, Raath noted the discovery of nine fragmentary carnivorous teeth near the pelvic region of the skeleton. He argued that the Vulcanodon carcass could have been embedded with the head and neck bent backward over the pelvis, a posture called a death pose that is frequently seen in dinosaur skeletons.
facts.quote: Raath en 1972 notó el descubrimiento de nueve dientes carnívoros fragmentarios cerca de la región pélvica del esqueleto. Argumentó que el cadáver de Vulcanodon podría haber sido incrustado con la cabeza y el cuello doblados hacia atrás por encima de la pelvis, una postura llamada pose de muerte que se ve con frecuencia en los esqueletos de dinosaurios.

facts.statement: However, as Cooper demonstrated in 1984, these teeth do not belong to Vulcanodon but to a theropod dinosaur that may have scavenged the Vulcanodon carcass.
facts.quote: Sin embargo, como lo demostró Cooper en 1984, estos dientes no pertenecen a Vulcanodon sino a un dinosaurio terópodo que pudo haber hurgado en el cadáver de Vulcanodon.

facts.statement: Michael Raath originally described Vulcanodon in 1972 as an advanced specialized prosauropod rather than a sauropod.
facts.quote: Originalmente, Michael Raath en 1972 describió a Vulcanodon no como un saurópodo sino como un prosaurópodo avanzado y especializado

facts.statement: Arthur Cruickshank was the first to demonstrate in 1975 that Vulcanodon was actually a sauropod.
facts.quote: Arthur Cruickshank en 1975 fue el primero en demostrar que Vulcanodon era de hecho un saurópodo

facts.statement: Vulcanodon is now universally accepted as one of the most basal members of Sauropoda.
facts.quote: Hoy en día, Vulcanodon es universalmente aceptado como uno de los miembros más basales de Sauropoda

facts.statement: Michael Cooper erected the new family Vulcanodontidae in 1984.
facts.quote: Michael Cooper en 1984 erigió una nueva familia, Vulcanodontidae

facts.statement: Paul Upchurch showed in 1995 that Vulcanodontidae was polyphyletic and therefore invalid because Barapasaurus was more closely related to advanced sauropods than to Vulcanodon.
facts.quote: Paul Upchurch en 1995 mostró que Barapasaurus estaba más estrechamente relacionado con saurópodos posteriores y más avanzados que con Vulcanodon, lo que hace que Vulcanodontidae sea polifilético y por lo tanto inválida

facts.statement: Ronan Allain and colleagues discovered in 2004 and 2008 that Vulcanodon is more closely related to Tazoudasaurus.
facts.quote: Ronan Allain y sus colegas tanto en 2004 como en 2008 descubrieron que Vulcanodon está más estrechamente relacionado con Tazoudasaurus

facts.statement: Adam Yates described a single sauropod tail vertebra from the Upper Elliot Formation of South Africa in 2004 that may belong to a genus closely related to Vulcanodon.
facts.quote: Adam Yates en 2004 describió una sola vértebra de cola de saurópodo de la Formación Elliot superior de Sudáfrica que puede pertenecer a un género estrechamente relacionado con Vulcanodon

facts.statement: Adam Yates demonstrated in 2004 that Vulcanodon dates to the upper Lower Jurassic during the Toarcian, approximately 175-183 million years ago.
facts.quote: Adam Yates en 2004 ha demostrado recientemente que Vulcanodon es en realidad mucho más joven de lo que se pensaba anteriormente, que data de la parte superior del Jurásico Inferior durante el Toarciense, hace aproximadamente 175-183 millones de años

facts.statement: Vulcanodon comes from the "Vulcanodon Beds", a fossil-bearing sediment unit within the Batoka Formation.
facts.quote: Vulcanodon proviene de los "lechos de Vulcanodon", una unidad de sedimentos con fósiles dentro de la Formación Batoka

facts.statement: Cooper noted in 1984 that the habitat was desert-like, indicated by aeolian sands in the underlying Forest Sandstone Formation.
facts.quote: Cooper en 1984 señaló que el hábitat era desértico, como lo indican las arenas eólicas de la Formación Forest Sandstone, que subyace en los "lechos de Vulcanodon"

facts.statement: In 1984, Cooper pointed out that Vulcanodon lived in a desert environment and was therefore terrestrial, showing that sauropod gigantism did not evolve as an adaptation to aquatic life.
facts.quote: Inicialmente, se pensaba que los saurópodos eran principalmente acuáticos, habitaban exuberantes pantanos de turba y estaban cautivos de la flotabilidad del agua para soportar su peso corporal gigante. En 1984, Cooper señaló que Vulcanodon , el saurópodo más primitivo conocido en ese momento, vivía en un ambiente desértico y, por lo tanto, debe haber sido terrestre
